programme: SMAD2 as the core TGF-β effector, with KLF10 acting as its feedback regulator (KLF10's own target list is dominated by SMAD2, SMAD3, SMAD4, SMAD7 and TGFB1) and TSC22D1 as a canonical TGF-β-inducible early-response gene — together a TGF-β/SMAD2 signaling module rather than a generic stress or immune programme.
role_in_a: In Huntington's Disease, SMAD2-mediated TGF-β signaling is reported to enforce quiescence of adult hippocampal neural stem cells (PMID 20535034); KLF10 and TSC22D1 are the expected SMAD-responsive feedback and early-response layer of that same signal, though neither is independently placed in HD in this record.
role_in_b: In thyroid cancer, the same SMAD2/TGF-β axis is repeatedly described as a driver of epithelial-mesenchymal transition, invasion and dedifferentiation in papillary thyroid carcinoma — engaged downstream of GOLPH3 (42301509), ASAP1 (40742091), the CXCR7-TAGLN2 complex (41169389), and cancer-associated fibroblasts (41761234).
shared_axis: TGF-β/SMAD2 signaling is a general tissue-remodeling and differentiation-control pathway that appears to be redeployed in both settings: as a brake on stem-cell exit from quiescence in the HD-affected neurogenic niche, and as an EMT/invasion driver in thyroid tumor cells, with KLF10 and TSC22D1 forming the SMAD-responsive feedback layer common to both.
reasoning: SMAD2 is independently documented in both diseases in this record — once for HD (neurogenic-niche quiescence) and four times for thyroid cancer (EMT/invasion/dedifferentiation) — and it sits in a module with two factors (KLF10, TSC22D1) that are structurally SMAD-linked by their own target lists, so the module is nameable and partly evidenced rather than assembled from a single subgroup. It falls short of 'strong' because KLF10 and TSC22D1 have no literature placement in either disease here, and no source states an HD-thyroid connection through this axis directly — the cross-disease link is inference from each disease's separate TGF-β literature, not a retrieved fact.
support: PMID 20535034 — TGF-β/SMAD signaling maintains hippocampal neural stem cell quiescence, relevant to HD's neurogenic niche; PMID 42301509 — GOLPH3 promotes papillary thyroid carcinoma via TGF-β/SMAD signaling; PMID 41169389 — CXCR7-TAGLN2 complex regulates PTC invasion via this pathway; PMID 40742091 — ASAP1 drives EMT in PTC by activating TGF-β signaling; PMID 41761234 — cancer-associated fibroblasts drive thyroid dedifferentiation via TGF-β-linked signaling.
how_to_falsify: Block TGF-β receptor/SMAD2 signaling (e.g. SB431542 or SMAD2 knockdown) in parallel in HD patient-derived neural stem cells and in papillary thyroid carcinoma lines, and measure TGF-β-driven induction of KLF10 and TSC22D1 in both; if SMAD2 loss fails to affect neural stem cell quiescence exit in the HD model, or KLF10/TSC22D1 are not TGF-β-inducible in either cell type, the shared-module account is wrong.
caveats: The HD-side network here is built from blood, not brain tissue, so the neurogenic-niche role attributed to SMAD2 in HD is supported by only one external paper, not by what this blood network itself shows; concordance is reported across 483 patient-group comparisons but only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the fraction reflects within-cohort subgroup robustness more than independent replication. Several generic inflammatory/stress TFs (IRF7, NFKB2, RELB, FOXO1, DDIT3) and SP1 were removed as tissue-generic, which is reassuring against a generic-binding artifact but also means this account should not be extended into an inflammation story. HEY2, NFE2L2, CREB1, AIP and the remaining factors have real thyroid- or HD-specific citations individually but no counterpart evidence on the other disease side in this record, so they were left out of the carrying set rather than forced into the programme.
